name: Luren
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hölzl, Andreas 2021. The Lu(ren) language of Guizhou, China (comparative/wordlist article; the only linguistic description). No open full text located.

sources.citation: Hölzl, Andreas. 2026. Studies in East Asian Comparative Linguistics. Cumulative habilitation thesis, frontmatter (43 pp.), University of Potsdam. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20507926. Sections 2.6.2 'Lujia' and 2.6.3 'Areal typology', pp. 31-32.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent anywhere in the 43 pp. (grep for stress/accent/prosod: no hits for any Ta-Li language). On Lujia phonology it gives only inventory counts, p. 32: 'at least 7 [vowels] in Lujia', 'no [final consonants] in Lujia', 'at least 4 [tones] in Lujia (study 14 Hölzl & Hölzl 2025), not including sandhi phenomena that mostly remain unclear for now'; Luren B 'appears to have a larger inventory of tones' and 'exhibits final nasals'. States (p. 32) that all reliable data are six wordlists and 'almost nothing can be said about Lujia' beyond the lexicon.
Bibliographic pointers only (Hölzl & Hölzl 2025, Hölzl 2021 a/d, GPECC 1982/1984, Guizhou Ethnic Gazetteer 2002, Dafang County Gazetteer 1996, Zhao Weifeng 2011); no phonology.

sources.citation: Hölzl, Andreas. 2021. Longjia (China) - Language Contexts. Language Documentation and Description 20: 13-34. DOI 10.25894/ldd29 (CC-BY-NC).
sources.note: Article is about Longjia; Luren appears only comparatively. p. 17: 'Luren is only recorded in brief wordlists (see Hölzl 2021)'; Luren forms cited with tone numbers (Qianxi ta31 'two', li31 'pig'); p. 16: Longjia is related to Luren (about 58% lexical parallels out of 140 items, GMSWSB 1984: 40-42). No mention of stress or accent for any language; only a Pojiao Longjia tone inventory (55, 33, 13, 31, p. 24).
